design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (death benefit chain). Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 4, 6]; the renewal takes 4 factors, the valuation interest 5, the settlement 6.

1. Why this is a good test. A beneficiary asks only for her share of her late father's annuity as a lump sum. A correct agent must (a) see that the SecureRate 3 guarantee period ended 2026-08-20 and was never renewed, (b) read in the valuation rule that the valuation interest waits on the renewed rate for a period that ended before the valuation date, (c) record the default renewal at 0.0480 (four factors, one deciding the band from the date-of-death value because the owner died before the renewal date), (d) value the death benefit with interest to 2026-08-27 — the date Ashgrove first held a certified certificate, on the owner's whole life claim — split at the renewal date (16,630.71), and (e) work her share (reallocated because co-primary Daniel died first, shown by the term policy the owner held on his life) and the claim interest (1,789.58) and hand her the lump-sum election. Difficulty sits in reading rules, reconciling four products' records and arithmetic; one tool per problem.

2. Scope. Occupied by task 0: fixed_ext_missed_withdrawal_charge, fixed_ext_surrender_part_year_interest, fixed_ext_surrender_value and their three tools. Task 1 claims fixed_ext_claim_renewal_rate, fixed_ext_death_valuation_interest, fixed_ext_death_claim_settlement and renew_guarantee_period_14f04954, credit_death_valuation_interest_0cf0ffa2, settle_death_benefit_share_569ae0ca. Union = all six extended policies; no overlap. Task 1 is the last task, nothing is reserved.

3. Problem-tree card. Root A = fixed_ext_death_claim_settlement (user tool). Edge A -> B (fixed_ext_death_valuation_interest): value_input, gate s_db, form state, sentence "A beneficiary's death benefit share is not paid until the contract carries the valuation interest credited through the valuation date of the death benefit." (negated: a payment waits on a booked credit). Only B's write creates an interest entry whose period closes on the valuation date. Seed proof: latest interest entry a2c1bc6b-8aed-427b-92bd-d71e1662463c closes 2025-08-20. Edge B -> C (fixed_ext_claim_renewal_rate): value_input, gate v_growth, form state, sentence "The death benefit valuation interest is fixed only after the contract carries its renewed guaranteed rate for every guarantee period that ended before the valuation date." (affirmative). Only C's write moves the guarantee period end and sets the renewed rate. Seed proof: guarantee_period_end_date 2026-08-20 < valuation date 2026-08-27, rate 0.0555, schedule start 2023-08-21. Order C, B, A (chain). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip B -> claim interest 1,690.92 (gold 1,789.58); skip C -> valuation interest 16,666.01 (gold 16,630.71). User tool: the lump-sum election is the beneficiary's own act, completed on the spot. Four-point test passed for both sentences (ordering connective, record-visible state, no code token, hard requirement matching condition). Derivations: contract shows an expired period without renewal + the renewal rule (records the renewed rate and dates) -> C; no interest entry closing on the valuation date + the valuation rule -> B.

4. Base-invariant card. Step 13 subject fixed_guarantee_period_renewed: fixed_interest_crediting (no gate) and fixed_guarantee_period_renewal, whose election-in-window time gate is superseded by the renewal policy's overwrite (a default renewal needs no election); no election is on file. Step 15 subject fixed_interest_credited: fixed_interest_crediting, policy_scope. Step 17 subject fixed_death_benefit_paid: fixed_death_benefit.proof_and_approval (claim 0a7e3821-4008-4f16-b199-67267adab359: certificate received true, status approved) and disbursement_status (contract status death_claim_pending). Rachel is a primary beneficiary of the designation in effect at death (signed 2023-08-14, only designation); she is an adult; a non-spouse beneficiary may take a lump sum. Overwrites declared: renewal band clause and election gate; due-proof valuation clause and guarantee-period rate clause; claim-interest clause.

5. Business-object card. Contract FA42295071 (53d65c8a-8f1a-4a91-baba-f292f6041add), claim 0a7e3821-4008-4f16-b199-67267adab359 (Rachel). Rows read: two anniversary credits (last 2025-08-21 at 0.0555), three designation lines (50/30/20), no withdrawals; whole life WL41187340 claim certificate 2026-08-27 and payment 2026-09-02, premiums (9 in window); income IA41520936 installments (9 in window); term LT41968205 on Daniel J. Mercer, death 2025-12-03. Ellen's 20 percent share (pro rata 28.571 percent) stays on the contract.

6. Factor card. C: measure date -> date-of-death value 299,155.71 (baseline renewal-date value 300,842.74 gives 0.049); band mid 0.002 (baseline 0.0475); persistency 0.0015 (0.0465); whole life relationship partial 0.0005 (0.0475) [cross whole; the rule counts a whole life policy on record whatever its status]; all baseline 0.0455. B: valuation date 2026-08-27 from the whole life certificate (17,155.36) [cross whole]; two-part split (14,491.32); value band 0.0005 (16,485.73); age addition 0.001 (16,340.74); income relationship 0.0005 (16,485.73) [cross income]; all baseline 14,411.03. A: start from claim receipt (2,295.33); base rate 0.05 (1,376.60); late addition 0.01 (1,514.26); coordination 0.005 (1,651.92) [cross whole]; check extension 3 days, parameter (1,672.87); divisor 360, parameter (1,765.06); all baseline 1,157.03. Near misses: whole life premiums and income installments of 2025-07 to 2025-10 fall outside the 12-month windows; the renewal-date value (300,842.74) would put the band on the jumbo tier, which the date-of-death measure excludes.

7. World rows and automatic clauses. Owner Franklin D. Mercer (deceased 2026-07-14), caller Rachel Mercer-Lindqvist (5025550118, SSN 8122, ZIP 40206, DOB 1971-04-11). The contract has no withdrawals, no systematic plan and no RMD (non-qualified). The whole life and term claims are completed and paid; the income annuity completed at death (Life Only); nothing in another product is left owing. The only open items on the contract are the unrecorded renewal, the unvalued death benefit and the beneficiaries' shares; Ellen's share is not part of this call.

8. Persona. Brisk, grieving pharmacist; volunteers only the request (her share as a lump sum) and that her claim was approved; credentials, contract number, name spelling and payout preference only on request; her brother's death only if asked about other beneficiaries; passive consent to whatever must be taken care of first; runs the election with the figures read to her; closes when told the check is on its way.

9. Standard solution and verification (actual handling-time recomputation with the real tools): step 13 renewal_rate 0.0480; step 15 interest_amount 16,630.71 (valuation_date 2026-08-27); step 17 claim_interest 1,789.58 with share_amount 215,467.59 and payout check. Per-task gates OK.

10. Draft recomputation from the visible context alone: the settlement rule waits on the valuation interest; the valuation rule waits on the renewed rate for any period ended before the valuation date; the contract shows such a period; the renewal rule's ladders give 0.0480; the valuation rule gives 371 days split 365/6 = 16,630.71; the settlement rule gives 71.428571 percent of 301,654.62 and 46 days at 6.5 percent over 360 = 1,789.58 — identical to gold.

Revision log: (r1) the valuation tool records the valuation date as the interest period end so the claim interest can start from it (tool arg valuation_date).

Rework round 2 (policy-task audit): F-C2 — P6's prerequisite sentence now waits on 'the valuation interest credited through the valuation date of the death benefit', the same date P5's valuation-date ladder fixes (all three tiers), and the edge condition names that date; the base phrase 'date due proof of death was received' is no longer used. F-C3 — claim_interest_end_extension and claim_interest_day_count relabelled parameter (tiers give +3/+1/+0 days and divisor 360/366/365); P6 now carries 5 parameter and 1 method factors. O-C7 — P4's relationship tiers now read 'has an Ashgrove whole life policy on record, whatever its current status', removing the present-tense reading. Observation 6 — the unverifiable historical-rate decomposition was removed from the seed check. Scored values unchanged: 0.0480 / 16,630.71 / 1,789.58 (share 215,467.59); gates re-run green.
user_scenario: You are Rachel Mercer-Lindqvist, 55, a hospital pharmacist in Louisville, calling on your lunch break. You are brisk and organised but still raw from losing your father, Franklin, in July, so you keep the call practical and a little clipped. You open by explaining that your father had an Ashgrove annuity, that you are one of his beneficiaries, that you sent in the claim form with the death certificate and got a letter saying the claim was approved, and that you would like your share paid out to you now as a lump sum. When asked how to find you, you give your own phone number, 5025550118. To confirm who you are, and only when asked, you give your date of birth, April 11, 1971 (1971-04-11), the last four of your Social Security number, 8122, and your ZIP code, 40206. If asked for the contract number you read it from the approval letter: FA42295071. If asked your name as it should appear, you spell it: Rachel Mercer-Lindqvist. If asked how you want to be paid you say: By check, mailed to my house, like I put on the claim form. Only if the representative asks about the other beneficiaries do you say that your brother Daniel passed away last December and your sister Ellen is dealing with her own share separately; you do not know what anyone's share comes to. You do not know what the annuity is worth; you have not seen a statement since your father died. You tell the representative that whatever Ashgrove needs to do on its side to pay you properly is fine with you; if the representative says something else has to be taken care of on the contract before your payment, you say to go ahead. When the representative explains the lump-sum election and hands you the step to accept it, you carry it out yourself using exactly the contract number, claim number, name, amounts and payment method the representative reads to you, and you read back the confirmation. When the representative confirms your share and the interest are on their way by check, you thank them, say you appreciate the help, and end the call. You never tell the representative what to check or how to calculate anything.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.fixed_contract_id: Value 53d65c8a-8f1a-4a91-baba-f292f6041add. Basis: the claim record names the contract and the contract lookup returns FA42295071; docstring: 'the SecureRate contract whose guarantee period renews, read from the contract lookup'. Uniqueness: the claim concerns one contract.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.renewal_rate: Value 0.0480. current_base_rate (SecureRate 3) 0.0440. Measured renewal value: the owner died 2026-07-14, before the renewal date 2026-08-21 -> measured on the date of death: 285,023.91 x 1.0555^(327/365) = 299,155.71 (baseline: renewal-date value 300,842.74). Band: 299,155.71 is at least 250,000 but under 300,000 -> mid_addition 0.002 (baseline standard band 0.0015; on the renewal-date value the ladder would give 0.003). Persistency: first guarantee period since issue (schedule start = issue date) and no withdrawal ever -> 0.0015. Whole life relationship: the owner's WL41187340 shows 9 premium payments in the 12 months before 2026-10-22 -> 0.0005. Rate = 0.0440 + 0.002 + 0.0015 + 0.0005 = 0.0480, above the 0.0100 minimum.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the tool that credits death benefit valuation interest.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Credit the death benefit valuation interest of 16630.71 closing on 2026-08-27, raising the contract value to 301,654.62.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: fixed_ext_death_valuation_interest (state_due once the death claim is on file): the beneficiary's share is not paid until the contract carries the valuation interest.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.fixed_contract_id: Value 53d65c8a-8f1a-4a91-baba-f292f6041add. Basis: the deceased owner's contract from the claim and the contract lookup. Uniqueness: single contract on the claim.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.interest_amount: Value 16630.71. Contract value 285,023.91, last credit 2025-08-21 at 0.0555. Valuation date: a certified certificate was received on the owner's whole life claim on 2026-08-27, before this claim (2026-09-09) -> 371 days (baseline 384 days to 2026-09-09). Split: the guarantee period ended 2026-08-20 within the period and 2026-08-27 is 6 days after the renewal date (within 30) -> 365 days at the expiring 0.0555 and 6 days at the renewed 0.0480. Additions to each rate: value band 0.0005 (285,023.91 between 250,000 and 300,000), age 0.001 (aged 80 at death, held 2 whole years), income relationship 0.0005 (9 installments in 12 months) = 0.002. Interest = 285,023.91 x (1.0575^(365/365) x 1.0500^(6/365) - 1) = 16,630.71.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.valuation_date: Value 2026-08-27. Basis: the valuation date rule — 'where a certified death certificate for the owner was received on an Ashgrove whole life claim before this contract's death claim was received, the date that certificate was received'; the whole life claim record shows received_date 2026-08-27 with death_certificate_received true, and this claim was received 2026-09-09. Docstring: 'the date the death benefit is valued on, which closes the interest period, written YYYY-MM-DD'. Uniqueness: the late-claim tier does not apply (claim 57 days after death) and the earlier certificate exists, so no other date qualifies.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_interest: Value 1789.58. edges.condition: The contract shows an interest credit entry whose interest period closes on the valuation date of the death benefit, credited after the owner's death claim was received, and the contract value includes it.
edges.policy_source: A beneficiary's death benefit share is not paid until the contract carries the valuation interest credited through the valuation date of the death benefit.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-10-22 the contract's most recent interest credit is the 2025-08-21 anniversary credit; nothing has been credited for the period up to the valuation date, so the contract value 285,023.91 is not yet the death benefit.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The valuation interest credit (16,630.71, period closing 2026-08-27) adds an interest entry whose period ends on the valuation date and raises the contract value to 301,654.62.

edges.condition: The contract's guarantee period end date is not earlier than the valuation date, its guaranteed rate is the rate of the renewed period, and its surrender charge schedule start date is the renewal date.
edges.policy_source: The death benefit valuation interest is fixed only after the contract carries its renewed guaranteed rate for every guarantee period that ended before the valuation date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The SecureRate 3 guarantee period ended 2026-08-20, before the 2026-08-27 valuation date, but the contract still shows that end date, the expiring rate 0.0555 and the 2023-08-21 schedule start: the renewal was never recorded.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Recording the default renewal sets the guaranteed rate to 0.0480, the guarantee period end to 2029-08-20 and the schedule start (renewal date) to 2026-08-21.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (settlement <- valuation interest <- renewal); no problem has two prerequisites, so no parallel pair can be reordered. The order is entailed by the two prerequisite sentences: the valuation interest waits on the renewed rate for a guarantee period that ended before the valuation date, and the share is not paid until the valuation interest is credited.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the valuation credit leaves the contract value at 285,023.91 and the latest interest period end at 2025-08-20: claim interest 1,690.92 instead of 1,789.58 (and the share 203,588.51 instead of 215,467.59); the terminal ledger lacks the valuation entry.

Skipping the renewal leaves the expiring rate and the 2023 schedule start: valuation interest 16,666.01 instead of 16,630.71 (every day at 0.0555 plus additions), and the terminal contract keeps the stale guarantee period.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for her share paid as a lump sum. It never mentions a renewal, a guarantee period, interest, a valuation date, a certificate on another policy or any crediting; her only related line is passive — if the representative says something else has to be taken care of on the contract before her payment, she says to go ahead. Her brother's death is given only if the representative asks about the other beneficiaries.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: settle_death_benefit_share_569ae0ca creates the payment entry, lowers the contract value and records the election with whatever amounts are passed; it never looks for a valuation entry. credit_death_valuation_interest_0cf0ffa2 creates the interest entry without looking at the guarantee period. renew_guarantee_period_14f04954 only updates the rate and dates. None returns an error or a hint when a prerequisite is unresolved (no conditions in task_tools.py).

the owner died 2026-07-14, before the 2026-08-21 renewal date -> measured on the date of death
first guarantee period since issue AND no withdrawal ever -> first_period_addition
